Member, Board of Directors (Lead Independent Director from Nov. 2025; former Chair, Strategy and Acquisitions Committee)

background_rationale: Spent about 35 years at Procter & Gamble in sales and customer marketing leadership, retiring as Global Sales Officer, before moving from Tyson's board into the CEO role.

notable.summary: Tyson's board named Schomburger, a director since 2016 and lead independent director, to succeed Donnie King as president and CEO effective Oct. 4, 2026; the stock fell more than 4.5% in early trading on the news.
In announcing his appointment, Schomburger said he aimed to strengthen Tyson's brands with superior products and capitalize on emerging opportunities through AI acceleration.
Joined Tyson as an employee on July 1, 2026, for a three-month transition period working alongside King before taking over at the end of the fiscal year.

personal_story.hook: After 35 years selling for Procter & Gamble, Jeff Schomburger moved from Tyson's boardroom to its CEO chair.
personal_story.summary: Schomburger is a Florida native who graduated with honors in economics from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. He built his career at Procter & Gamble in sales and customer marketing, including international assignments and leading P&G's global team serving Walmart, and retired in 2019 as Global Sales Officer. He joined Tyson Foods' board in 2016 and became its lead independent director before being named CEO, a move local press noted brought in a leader with no prior operating experience in food processing.

open_issues: Effective date conflict: Tyson press release (May 28, 2026) says Oct. 4, 2026; Wikipedia's Tyson Foods article says Oct. 5, 2026. Kept seed/press-release date 2026-10-04. No post-effective confirmation found, though Tyson's leadership page now lists him as President & CEO.
P&G tenure length differs: press release says 35 years; Tyson bio says 'more than 30 years'. P&G start year and dates of individual P&G roles not found; left null.
Degree type at UNC-Chapel Hill stated only as 'bachelor's degree in economics'; recorded as BA (UNC economics is a BA program) but not explicitly confirmed. Graduation year unknown.

Talk Business describes him as 'global sales officer for P&G's Walmart business in his final decade', while Tyson describes Global Sales Officer and President of the Global Walmart team as separate roles.
